title: EPFO Confirms Your EPF Interest Rate for FY 2025-26: What It Means for Your Savings
description: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has confirmed the 8.25% interest rate for your EPF account for the financial year 2025-26. This rate ensures.

faq.q: Who decides the EPF interest rate?
faq.a: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the EPFO recommends the interest rate, which is then formally approved and notified by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

faq.q: When will the 8.25% interest for FY 2025-26 be credited?
faq.a: The government ratified the 8.25% interest rate for FY 2025-26 in June 2026. The interest is expected to be credited to subscriber accounts shortly after this ratification, often within the same month or soon thereafter.

faq.q: How can I check my EPF balance and the credited interest?
faq.a: You can easily check your EPF balance and view your passbook online through the EPFO Member e-Sewa portal, by using the UMANG mobile app, by sending an SMS to 7738299899, or by giving a missed call to 9966044425 from your registered mobile number.

faq.q: What happens if I withdraw my EPF money before retirement?
faq.a: EPF withdrawals are generally allowed under specific conditions like retirement, unemployment, or for certain emergencies such as medical expenses, purchasing a home, or children's education. Premature withdrawals before completing five years of service might lead to the interest earned becoming taxable.

faq.q: Is the EPF interest rate likely to change soon?
faq.a: The 8.25% interest rate has been maintained for the third consecutive financial year (FY 2023-24, FY 2024-25, and FY 2025-26), showing a period of stability. Any future changes would be part of the annual review process by the CBT and the Ministry of Finance.

fact_check.summary: The article is largely reliable, accurately reporting the EPF interest rate for FY 2025-26 and general EPF rules. However, it contains a few inaccuracies regarding the crediting date of interest and the number of contributing members.

corrections.note: Corrected the date of government ratification and the date of interest credit for FY 2025-26 based on verified sources.

edits.why: The original statement about the government ratifying the rate in June 2026 was not consistently supported across all sources. The CBT recommended the rate in March 2026, and the Ministry of Finance approved it, with the credit occurring on July 15, 2026.
